subject: Request: temporary billing allowance for ML integration delay (Atlas AI)
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>
To: Grace Oconnor <grace@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>
Cc: 
Date: 2026-04-12T09:12:00Z
Subject: Request: temporary billing allowance for ML integration delay (Atlas AI)

Hi Grace / Marcus —

Quick context: Atlas AI (Samir Patel) has been onboarding a big LLM feature that depends on our private embeddings endpoint. Engineering has pushed the embeddings GA for their workspace out ~6 weeks and Atlas is asking for a billing concession while they wait — they’re worried about the cost of holding warm capacity and the perceived value while the feature is incomplete.

They've explicitly asked for a temporary credit/discount to bridge the gap and avoid churn. I pushed back on blanket reductions, but Samir said they’ll need something concrete to keep the renewal on track (deal in negotiation, see DEAL-4839).

Ask: can we approve a temporary commercial allowance to keep the deal moving? I propose one of the options below (open to trade-offs):
- Option A: 30% credit on hosted usage for 3 months (no retroactive billing).
- Option B: 20% credit + commitment to extend Dedicated trial by 1 month.
- Cap: either option capped at $35k total credit.

Why now: Atlas is showing signs of pause in procurement; legal/finance want something documented fast. Engineering (Marcus) flagged the embedding ETA as delayed due to a dependency in the KV cache refactor — Marcus, can you confirm the ETA and whether we can accelerate?

Attachments: atlas-credit-proposal-2026-04-12.pdf (draft we can share)

Below is the customer's note for context (redacted):

We’re incurring storage and warm-up costs on our side and are not comfortable running full spend without the promised feature. Given the delay, we need a short-term commercial allowance while we keep the integration and plan the go-live. What flexibility can Redwood provide?

—Samir

1) What exact revenue at risk (ARR/TCV) if Atlas churns or reduces scope?
2) What is the engineering ETA and risk (can this slip further?)
3) Proposed guardrails for the credit (duration, cap, tie to usage thresholds / signed amendment).
4) Any precedent we should align to (other recent credits / exec exceptions)?

Marcus — can you confirm the technical timeline and whether we can ship a minimal embeddings surface sooner (opt-in beta) to reduce the business ask?

If numbers look small relative to deal value, I'm ok to approve a short-term allowance with finance sign-off. If it's material, we should route to Evelyn for exec approval.

Subject: Re: Request: temporary billing allowance for ML integration delay (Atlas AI)

Short answer: the embeddings work is delayed by ~6 weeks. More detail below.

Root cause: during the KV cache refactor we discovered a regression in memory fragmentation that impacts long-lived prefix caches (affects private embeddings for multi-tenant flows). The fix requires backporting a new allocator strategy and extra e2e tests.

ETA (realistic): target ship May 28, 2026 (we can try to compress to mid-May but that risks a rollback).

Mitigations:
- We can offer an opt-in developer beta for a subset of Atlas's workspaces within 2–3 weeks that provides a limited embeddings surface (no guaranteed SLA).
- We cannot guarantee full production performance before late May without additional headcount/priority.

Implication: if Atlas needs full GA-grade embeddings to justify spend, the ask for credit is reasonable; if they’ll accept beta access we can reduce or eliminate the credit.

I attached the sprint summary: engine-roadmap-sprint-summary-2026-04-13.pdf.

-Marcus
Director, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>
To: Grace Oconnor <grace@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>

Date: 2026-04-13T12:30:00Z
Subject: Re: Request: temporary billing allowance for ML integration delay (Atlas AI)

Thanks Marcus — that ETA is helpful. Per customer conversations, Atlas wants a clear, timeboxed commitment before they finalize procurement. Based on the risk profile, my commercial proposal (to share with Atlas if you greenlight) is: 

- Proposal we present to Atlas: 30% credit on hosted usage for 3 months from go-live milestone or from the date the credit is granted (whichever is earlier).
- Hard cap of $30k total credit.
- Condition: credit is one-time, non-recurring and requires a signed amendment to the MSA stating the credit terms and acceptance of the projected GA date.
- Alternative (if we need to be more conservative): 25% credit for 2 months, capped at $20k, and we offer opt-in beta access within 2 weeks.

Rationale: gives Atlas runway to keep integration active, and the cap protects revenue. We can present the draft (attached) and ask for Finance quick review.

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwood.ai>
To: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>, Grace Oconnor <grace@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>
Cc: Finance Team <finance@redwood.ai>, Legal Team <legal@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-04-14T15:48:00Z
Subject: Re: Request: temporary billing allowance for ML integration delay (Atlas AI)

Thanks for the clear context. Given the timeline and the traction at Atlas (DEAL-4839) I will approve a constrained commercial concession with these firm guardrails: 

1) Approved concession: 25% credit for 2 months, capped at $20,000 total.
2) Condition: Credit is contingent on a signed amendment to the MSA that:
   - references the roadmap ETA (target May 28, 2026)
   - states credit is one-time and non-recurring
   - requires Atlas to accept the opt-in beta if it is offered before GA
3) Finance must create a one-time negative invoice/credit note; Legal to draft the amendment (please use the attached draft as start).
4) Priyom: share the amendment + our commercial summary with Atlas and request countersignature within 7 business days. If no countersign in 7 days, concession expires.

Rationale: this balances retention risk and sets a hard financial cap. If Atlas signs and continues, we’ll revisit expansion post-GA.

Grace / Marcus — please confirm you can meet the May 28 target (or that the opt-in beta timeline stands) and copy Finance/Legal on the final amendment.

Approved by,
Evelyn Hart
VP, Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced above: atlas-credit-proposal-2026-04-12.pdf, engine-roadmap-sprint-summary-2026-04-13.pdf
